newsitem.title: USA: Dlr ends higher in US, Indonesia rupiah hurts yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends higher in US, Indonesia rupiah hurts yen.

text.p: Dollar/yen led the way to a higher U.S. unit close amid concern that a Southeast Asian currency crisis may hurt Japan's fragile economy.

A broad yen slump commenced after Indonesia announced a de facto float of its currency on Thursday, following similar actions by neighboring countries in recent weeks. The rupiah fell about 5.0 percent overnight, to a record low.

Traders expressed worry Japan may be forced to let its own currency weaken to compete with other Pacific-Rim countries. Fears that weak export markets for Japan might limit its option to raise interest rates also weighed on the yen.

The dollar mostly brushed off reports on the U.S. economy in July, showing industrial production rose 0.2 percent and consumer prices rose 0.2 percent, both overall and when food and energy is subtracted.
In other cross trade, sterling jumped more than four yen before settling to near 186 yen.
The dollar rose to 1.5158/63 Swiss francs, from 1.5152/57 and was nearly flat at Canadian 1.3902/07 compared with C$1.3903/08.
The pound rose to $1.5910/20 from $1.5812/22 and the Australian dollar fell to $0.7410/15 from $0.7429/34.
